body:
Context: Read D-77 (points 3–5) and Spec 15 §28. Cite D-17, D-18 and D-61 point 4 as amended by D-77. Part A (computed changes_of) is done. Part 1 of Lock (agent_guard) is done.

Goal: human task actions lock only when they change code. Per D-77 point 5 (clarified): "moving into a final column" means undoing or settling a task's in-progress changes, and "cancel without undo" means cancelling a task that never had changes.

Note from Part 1 of Lock:
tasks::api still takes the scope locks for every human change. needs_lock, the retry inside op, the set_scope question, the README note on inbox/, and the D-77 point 5 wording are all still to do.

Steps:

Add board::needs_lock(root, parts, body) -> Result<bool>. It reads the task and workflow with no lock. It returns true for:
POST /tasks/{tid}/actions where the action has revert = true or to is a final column, and changes_of is non-empty or some scope store has board_before rows for the task;
POST /tasks/{tid}/questions/{qid}, when the question has settings and the answer is Approve. Confirm which project locks apply_settings needs.
Everything else returns false: create, PATCH, notes, stop, pause/resume, discuss, starts, scope, and plain answers.

tasks::api (tasks.rs ~219): call board::guard only when needs_lock is true. Remove the ponytail comment.
Race: inside op, run the check again before change. If a lock is needed but not held, return a private retry result, and api takes guard and runs it again. On the second attempt, keep the lock whatever the result, so the retry is bounded. op must never take a flock, because record_verification calls tasks::update while holding a project lock and that would deadlock.
set_scope (E7013): decide whether to lock the projects being *removed* from scope, which closes the paused-run gap. Otherwise document the gap.
Update the board::api comment (~1352). README: with no server, a CLI run's notes wait in inbox/ until the next serve. Fix the D-77 point 5 wording.
Tests:

Unit test for needs_lock:
false for stop, note, create, and cancel with no changes;
true for cancel after record, and for Approve on a settings question.
Acceptance: slow self-timed as in Task 1. After the marker appears, POST /tasks create, a note, and stop each finish in under 1 s.
Run rust-acceptance, rust-board-tests and rust-lockdown-tests.

The double create, the inbox restart and the /events reconnect tests already exist (board_acceptance.py lines 774, 786 and 758).

Lines may have changed since this report was written.
title: Task Store: Locks, part 2
